history.summary: DISTINCTNESS FLAG: this is the Samaleswari temple of Bolangir town — not the famous 16th-century Samaleswari temple of Sambalpur (which has its own dataset file 'samaleswari-temple-sambalpur'); the Orissa High Court case explicitly describes this one as the '16th Century Samaleswari Temple (in Balangir District)'. Local historical accounts say Maa Samaleswari was installed in Bolangir town by Narasingha Dev, the Chauhan ruler of the Patna state and elder brother of Balaram Dev of Sambalpur — making Samaleswari and Pataneswari (Patna's presiding deity) 'sister' goddesses — but the exact installation date is weakly sourced. She is the presiding deity (aaradhya) of western Odisha's Shakta-Shaiva-Vaishnava amalgam tradition, and the Balangir-town temple is an active worship centre with parking, prasad lunch and evening aarti reported by devotees. As of 2025, renovation/construction work is ongoing at the temple; the Orissa High Court directed authorities to rehabilitate a hereditary sevayat before eviction during the works. Coordinates from geocoder (matched 'Samaleswari Temple, Daily Market Road, Balangir' — consistent with 'middle of Balangir town' reviewer reports). MEDIA FLAG: no Balangir-town-specific image found in three image searches; all results depict the Sambalpur temple — media left empty rather than misattribute.
